To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Arabidopsis thalamus is able to respond to seasonal change by sensing day-length, or the photoperiod, and that this is accomplished by sensing photoperiod through the circadian clock and by the activity of CO, and that FT is the key protein that is produced in response to photoperoiodic conditions.

photoperiodic regulation of flowering is accomplished through the regulation of FT function in response to the day length, and that this regulation involves the circadian clock and other components of the floral transition pathway.

the photoperiodic flowering response in Arabidopsis is mediated by the regulation of the florigen gene FLOWERING LOCUs T (FT) through the action of the CO transcription factor, and that FT protein movement and interactions are critical for the photoperiod flowering response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate photoperiodic flowering in Arabidopsis.
elucidating how the plant senses the environment, and how this information is translated into a flowering response.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms that regulate FT function in response to photothermal and nutritional cues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of FT function is central to the photoperiodic regulation of the flowering time in Arabidopsis.

the photoperiodic regulation of flowering in Arabidopsis is mediated by a network of transcription factors, including CO, FLOWERING LOCUs M (FLM), FLOWERING LOCULS T (FT), and FLOWERING LOCU M C (FLC), and other components of the circadian clock and light signaling, as well as by the movement of the FT protein from the leaves to the shoot apex and the interaction between FT and its receptor, FD.

the photoperiodic regulation of flowering time in Arabidopsis is accomplished by a complex network of transcription factors and other regulatory proteins, which are themselves regulated by the photoperiod, the circadian clock and other environmental and endogenous factors, and that this network is able to integrate these inputs into the final output of flowering time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photoperiodic regulation is a complex process, involving the interplay between the clock, the photoperiodic network and environmental signals.
photoperiodic induction of flowering is a highly complex process, involving a number of different components, which are integrated into a coherent network.
photoperiodic flowering is a complex process that involves the integration of many different signals to determine the appropriate time of year to initiate the floral developmental program.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoperiodic flowering response is a dynamic process that is controlled by a complex network of interacting genes.
